title: H4087 (123rd General Assembly): Firearm and ammunition

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2019-02-26; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess123_2019-2020/prever/4087_20190226.htm (LegiScan doc 1930256))
provenance.note: Introduced version (Feb. 26, 2019); no later version or vote on file. Struck: "violent crime ... classified as a felony" (now any crime punishable by more than one year) and the old flat felony penalty (up to $2,000 / 5 years). Item (B) is quoted as the three penalty tiers only because the lead-in is spliced into struck text.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500): (A) It is unlawful for a person who has been convicted of a crime punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of more than one year to possess, ship, transport, or receive a firearm or ammunition within this State.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500): (1) misdemeanor for a first offense and must be imprisoned not more than three years; (2) felony for a second offense and must be imprisoned not more than ten years; and (3) felony for a third or subsequent offense and must be imprisoned not more than fifteen years.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-500): (E) A prior offense for purposes of this section means any conviction related to the possession, shipping, transporting, or receiving of a firearm or ammunition in this State, another state, or in violation of federal law.
